title: Move reusable website styles into shared component stylesheets
description:
The website still spreads a lot of reusable UI styling across page-local `<style>` blocks instead of shared component-owned stylesheets.

Current examples:
- `website/src/components/GameReplayView.astro` still owns a sizeable local style block for replay header and metadata UI.
- `website/src/pages/golden/[...slug].astro` and `website/src/pages/games/live.astro` both keep page-local style overrides around shared viewer structures.
- Large pages like `website/src/pages/season/[season]/results.astro` and `website/src/pages/season/[season]/rankings.astro` continue to define substantial UI styles inline.

Why this matters:
- Visual consistency drifts because similar controls and cards are styled in different files.
- Refactors have to touch many pages to make one visual change.
- It is harder to tell which styles belong to a reusable component versus a one-off page concern.

Suggested fix:
1. Identify the recurring UI primitives (header bars, control rows, badges, game cards, log panels, table controls).
2. Move their styles into shared stylesheets or component-scoped CSS next to the owning component.
3. Leave page-local styles only for truly page-specific layout.

The goal is a more consistent visual system and less CSS duplication, not a blind move of everything into one global file.
